newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish govt welcomes union approval of wage deal.
newsitem.headline: Irish govt welcomes union approval of wage deal.

text.p: The Irish government on Thursday welcomed the decision by the Irish Congress of Trade Unions (ICTU) to ratify Partnership 2000, the new national wage agreement.

"The Partnership puts in place the institutional infrastructure necessary to secure for Ireland, through improved competitiveness, continued economic and social progress," a government statement said.

The agreement provides for the maintenance of an environment which promises industrial peace, wage moderation and sound public finances as well as an equitable distribution of the benefits of growth to all sections of society, particularly the weak and most vulnerable, the government said.

Delegates at a special conference of the Irish Congress of Trade Unions (ICTU), the umbrella body representing all of Ireland's unions, voted by a margin of 83 votes to accept the new agreement earlier today.
There were 217 votes for the agreement and 134 against.
ICTU was the last of the 19 organisations which participated in the negotiations to give its approval to the new accord.
Partnership 2000 allows for wage rises of 9.25 percent over a three-year period and promises tax reductions of 1.0 billion punts ($1.6 billion) over the life of the accord.
The programme also sets targets for the public finances, aiming for a general government deficit of not more than 1.5 percent of GDP and a debt/GDP ratio of 70 percent by 1999.
